newsitem.title: USA: US Army rape trial deliberations enter fifth day.
newsitem.headline: US Army rape trial deliberations enter fifth day.

text.p: Military jurors in the court-martial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson resumed deliberations Tuesday for a fifth day of considering if the Army drill instructor is guilty of rape.
The six-member panel met for nine hours Monday, bringing the total time of deliberations at that point to 25 hours.

Simpson is charged with 19 counts of rape involving six female trainees at the Aberdeen Proving Ground's Ordnance Centre and School, plus 35 counts on charges including forceable sodomy, indecent assault, and maltreatment.

Simpson, 32, faces life in prison if convicted of rape. He has already pleaded guilty to 11 counts of consensual sex and five counts of propositioning for which he faces a maximum of 32 years in prison.

His is the highest profile case in a major sexual misconduct investigation at the base, which has become the military's biggest sexual harassment scandal since the Navy's 1991 Tailhook affair. Simpson is the first of 12 trainers facing various misconduct charges to go before a court-martial.
